captions.text: 1610: the Newfoundland colony.
c. 1610: Mempawah's government is founded at Pekana.

1610: the capital moves to Khirki, the new city of Malik Ambar, later Aurangabad (infobox 'Aurangabad (1610-1636)', 'Junnar (1610)'; Malik Ambar page: 'He founded/inhabited the city of Khirki in 1610').

Bikaner stayed its own state under Mughal suzerainty: 'The state of Bikaner was founded in 1465'; its rulers acknowledged Akbar's suzerainty (Kalyan Mal, 1542-1571) and served as Mughal generals (Rai Singh, 1571-1612).
1610: Cuper's Cove is founded in Newfoundland.
Summer 1610: many towns swear to him again.
Late 1610 (no month on the page): the Semiboyarshchina «изгнало воевод самозванца из Серпухова и Тулы».
1610: Anaukpetlun takes Toungoo.
early 17th century: Cayor becomes a Denianke tributary.
1610: Raja Wodeyar I takes Srirangapatna and moves the capital there.
1610: the capital moves from Mysore to Srirangapatna.
The Gambian suzerainty ends with the empire; the page gives no separate date.

c. 1610: the Mali Empire ends with Mahmud Keita IV. 'Around 1610, Mahmud Keita IV died'; 'No single Keita ever ruled Manden after Mahmud Keita IV's death, resulting in the end of the Mali Empire'; 'Kangaba became the last refuge of the Keita royal family'.
1610: the Fez line cedes Larache to Spain.
c. 1610: 'Raja Kudung then moved the center of his government from Sidiniang to Pekana' (the page's 'c. 1610' is approximate).
1610: Polish units enter Moscow ('In 1610, Polish units entered Moscow'; 'the Poles were allowed into Moscow on 8 October').
1610: the Tuʻi Kanokupolu line is created.
1610: Gowa forces Wajo to Islam.
1610: closed in the year it opens.
c. 1610: the Atahontaenrat (Tahontaenrat) join as the fourth nation.
1 September 1610: Jülich falls.
By early September 1610 the pretender's forces «отбили у поляков Козельск, Мещовск, Почеп и Стародуб».
1610: Polish troops occupy Moscow.
20 November 1610: Larache is ceded.
11 December 1610: the pretender is killed.
the Kaluga phase: his base at Kaluga, Tula and Severia (Bryansk, Orel), the towns that swore to him in 1610 (Kolomna, Kashira, Serpukhov, Borovsk, Suzdal, Galich, Vladimir) and the south-east
1611: the Nguyễn take Phú Yên, the land between the Cù Mông and Cả passes.
1611: Denmark-Norway attacks Sweden.
1611: a truce after the death of Charles IX ends the war; the infobox gives 'status quo ante bellum'.
1611: Esim Khan takes Tashkent.
1611: 'Portuguese forces, acting in the name of the pretender Mayadunne of Uva, captured Kandy'.
after 1610: Andriandahifotsy 'extended his authority northwards past the Mangoky River' and his sons took the coast 'up to the Tsongay region (now Mahajanga)'.
1611: the Nguyễn attack Panduranga.
1611: Portuguese forces capture Kandy.
1611: Salzburg.

1611: Amami Ōshima and the northern islands annexed.
1611: a truce after the death of Charles IX ends the war; the infobox gives 'status quo ante bellum', so Swedish Estonia is unchanged.
1611: Satsuma takes the Amami Islands.
21 May 1611: the Accord of Osterhusen.

2 June 1611: 'On 2 June 1611 Smolensk had finally fallen to the Poles' (Polish–Russian War (1609–1618) page; the same page also gives 13 June 1611 for the mine attack, 'The fortress fell on the same day': both June).
1611: the 1609-1611 siege is over (see the gain).
1611: Smolensk falls to the Poles.
1611: the Swedes take Novgorod.
1611: Gowa invades Bone.
1611: Bone submits and accepts Islam; Tenripalle To'Akkeppeyang reigns 1611-1626 (rulers' table).
1611: Gowa invades Bone.
1611: Bone accepts Islam, 'the last major Bugis kingdom to accept Islam, in 1611' (Bone page); 'By 1611 all southwest Sulawesi, including Makassar's Bugis rival Bone, had become Muslim' (Gowa page).
the domain with the Amami Islands that Satsuma annexed after the invasion of Ryukyu
1612: the Dutch build Fort Nassau at Moree, the first Dutch fort on the Gold Coast.
1612: the Swedish Empire begins with the reign of Gustavus Adolphus.
c. 1612: Golconda's shape grows by about 191 cells along the north-eastern coast, held by no Cliopatria state.
1612: the court returns from Prague to Vienna (the page: Prague was the capital 1583-1611).
1612 (bridging): the page gives no year for the Portuguese leaving Kandy after the 1611 capture; the kingdom continues under Senarat (1604-1635).
1612: Sylhet leaves the 1490 bridge.
1612-13: the Tsangpa ruler leads an expedition to Ngari (West Tibet) and subjugates Mangyül Gungthang.
1612 (Cliopatria's year, page unclear): Cliopatria drops about 147 Georgian cells west of Kartli from its Ottoman shape in 1612 and does not restore them until 1727.
1612 (bridging, page silent): the Portuguese leave Kandy.
1612: Honoré II begins to style himself Prince of Monaco.
1612: Iskandar Muda conquers Deli.

July 1612: 'The Mughal army and navy began its expedition from near Dhaka in the July 1612.'
September 1612: Johor overruns Pekan's suburbs.
1612: a Johor army attacks Pekan, Pahang's capital.

20 November 1612: the Treaty of Nasuh Pasha ends the first phase of the war of 1603-1618 ('The Treaty of Nasuh Pasha was signed on 20 November 1612'; it 'secured the 1555 borders envisaged by the Peace of Amasya'); the page's war runs to 1618 (a later war of 1616-1618 ends with the Treaty of Serav, also a Persian victory, on the Ottoman-Persian wars page).
4 November 1612: 'Commonwealth forces were eventually driven out' of Moscow.
20 November 1612: the Treaty of Nasuh Pasha.

20 January 1613: the Treaty of Knäred.

January 1613: Denmark holds Älvsborg and Gullberg until the ransom is paid (infobox 'Älvsborg temporarily controlled by Denmark (1613)').

January 1613: Denmark-Norway keeps Älvsborg and Gullberg until Sweden pays the ransom: infobox 'Älvsborg temporarily controlled by Denmark (1613)' and 'Sweden pays 1 million rixdollars as ransom for Älvsborg'.
April 1613: Anaukpetlun takes Syriam.
April 1613: Portuguese Syriam ends with de Brito's execution by impalement ('it took him three days to die').
